candidates.title: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Agentic LLM Serving
candidates.abstract: Key-value (KV) caches impose substantial memory pressure on large language model serving systems, requiring cache eviction when capacity is insufficient. Existing mechanisms typically evict KV from the ends of cached sequences to preserve prefix sharing across requests. However, agent workloads repeatedly reuse long histories across successive turns. Recomputing the KV cache for tokens near the end of a sequence is substantially more expensive than for earlier tokens because their attention computation involves longer histories. To address this problem, we propose preserving shared prefixes and evicting the KV cache from the beginning of the remaining history while retaining the cached suffix. We build Penelope around this strategy by co-designing the eviction policy, KV recomputation, and unified GPU-CPU cache management. Returning requests reuse the KV cache retained in GPU or CPU memory and recompute only missing segments while preserving reuse of the cached suffix. We implement Penelope in SGLang and evaluate it on three Qwen3 model sizes using real agent traces. Compared with SGLang, Penelope reduces mean time to first token by up to 60% and job completion time by up to 37% with a GPU-only cache, and by up to 76% and 60% with a two-tier GPU-CPU cache.
candidates.reason: Penelopeはエージェント型LLMサービングで共有接頭辞を保ちつつ履歴の先頭側KVを追い出す方針を採り、SGLang実装でGPU-CPUキャッシュ管理と再計算を共設計し、初回トークン遅延を最大60%削減したと要旨が具体的に示す直接のKVキャッシュ貢献である。

candidates.title: Mosaic Pruning: A Hierarchical Framework for Generalizable Pruning of Mixture-of-Experts Models
candidates.abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) architectures have enabled a new frontier in scaling Large Language Models (LLMs), offering superior performance by activating only a fraction of their total parameters during inference. However, their practical deployment is severely hampered by substantial static memory overhead, as all experts must be loaded into memory. Existing post-training pruning methods, while reducing model size, often derive their pruning criteria from a single, general-purpose corpus. This leads to a critical limitation: a catastrophic performance degradation when the pruned model is applied to other domains, necessitating a costly re-pruning for each new domain. To address this generalization gap, we introduce Mosaic Pruning (MoP). The core idea of MoP is to construct a functionally comprehensive set of experts through a structured ``cluster-then-select" process. This process leverages a similarity metric that captures expert performance across different task domains to functionally cluster the experts, and subsequently selects the most representative expert from each cluster based on our proposed Activation Variability Score. Unlike methods that optimize for a single corpus, our proposed Mosaic Pruning ensures that the pruned model retains a functionally complementary set of experts, much like the tiles of a mosaic that together form a complete picture of the original model's capabilities, enabling it to handle diverse downstream tasks.Extensive experiments on various MoE models demonstrate the superiority of our approach. MoP significantly outperforms prior work, achieving a 7.24\% gain on general tasks and 8.92\% on specialized tasks like math reasoning and code generation.
candidates.reason: Mosaic Pruningは全専門家をメモリに載せる必要があるMoEモデルの静的メモリ過多を対象に、専門家を機能的にクラスタリングして代表専門家を選ぶ階層的プルーニングで、単一コーパス由来の従来手法が他ドメインで劣化する問題を解消し、推論配備のメモリ削減に直接寄与する。

candidates.title: GLITCHES: GPU-FPGA LLM Inference Through a Collaborative Heterogeneous System
candidates.venue: IEEE Conference on High Performance Extreme Computing
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities across various tasks. However, in latency-sensitive scenarios, a small batch or even one batch is usually required. This leads to the prefill and the decode stage of LLM inference being computational and memory bottlenecks, respectively. Therefore, it is difficult for a homogeneous FPGA or GPU system to simultaneously address different computational bottlenecks in different stages of LLM inference, resulting in long prefill latency on FPGAs and low utilization during the decode stage on GPUs. This paper proposes GLITCHES, GPU-FPGA LLM inference through a collaborative heterogeneous system. In this paper, we analyze the different characteristics of GPUs and FPGAs and employ GPUs for the prefill stage and FPGAs for the decode stage, leveraging the strengths of GPUs and FPGAs. Based on HBM profiling results, we apply the data prefetching technique to further improve the off-chip memory bandwidth utilization during the decode computations on FPGAs. Experiments demonstrate that a GLITCHES heterogeneous LLM inference system with an A100 GPU and seven U280 FPGAs achieves a 1.28/1.34 times improvement in system throughput and a 2.38/1.90 times improvement in cost efficiency compared to a homogeneous system with 8-card A100/V100S GPUs.
candidates.reason: GLITCHESはLLM推論のプリフィルが計算律速、デコードがメモリ律速である特性に基づきGPUをプリフィル、FPGAをデコードに割り当てる協調型異種システムで、HBMプロファイリングに基づくデータプリフェッチによりデコード時の帯域利用を改善し、スループット向上を示している。

candidates.title: Plug-and-Play KV Cache Reuse for Low-Latency Retrieval-Augmented Generation
candidates.venue: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
candidates.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems often suffer from high latency during the prefilling stage, when large language models compute key–value (KV) caches for long prompts. Although caching shared documents can reduce redundant computation, directly reusing precomputed KV blocks typically causes substantial accuracy loss.In this work, we study KV cache reuse for RAG under a strictly plug-and-play regime, where the base language model is left unchanged and no retraining, prompt redefinition, or selective recomputation is performed. Within this setting, we propose a fine-tuning-free approach that reuses KV states across queries through an anchor-block and position-adjustment strategy. Our design preserves alignment with the model’s attention mechanism while enabling efficient recombination of cached blocks.Experiments on multiple QA benchmarks demonstrate up to a 5.9× reduction in time-to-first-token (TTFT) with only moderate accuracy degradation, demonstrating a practical efficiency–accuracy trade-off and establishing KV reuse as a promising path for real-time RAG applications where system simplicity and inference speed are the primary priorities.
candidates.reason: 本研究はRAGのプリフィル段階で共有文書のKVキャッシュを再利用するプラグアンドプレイ手法で、アンカーブロックと位置調整により再学習なしでKVブロックを再結合し、精度低下を抑えつつ初回トークン遅延を最大5.9倍削減する具体的な推論高速化を示している。

candidates.title: MambaOPU: An FPGA Overlay Processor for State-space-duality-based Mamba Models
candidates.abstract: State-space models (SSMs), such as Mamba, have emerged as a promising alternative to Transformers. However, the recently developed Mamba2, based on state space duality (SSD), is highly memorybound and suffers from limited computation efficiency. This inefficiency arises from its irregular broadcast element-wise multiplications and structured sparse computations. In this work, we propose MambaOPU, an FPGA overlay processor, to accelerate SSD. First, to reduce memory overhead, we introduce a software-hardware co-optimized operator fusion framework. Specifically, operator merging combines adjacent broadcast multiplication and summation operations into a single descriptor, while operator backward shifting embeds segment multiplication into subsequent operations. Both techniques shorten the computation path and improve computation efficiency. Second, to enhance sparse computation efficiency, we skip zero-region computations using a tensor-reorder-and-group algorithm combined with a sparse-predefined data fetcher. Additionally, since Mamba integrates linear operations with SSD, we develop a reconfigurable systolic array to improve data reuse across different computation modes. Extensive experiment results demonstrate that MambaOPU achieves up to $1812 \times$ and $880.79 \times$ higher normalized throughput and up to $12908 \times$ and $24.27 \times$ higher energy efficiency over Intel Xeon Gold 6348 CPU and NVIDIA A100 GPU, respectively.
candidates.reason: MambaOPUは状態空間双対性に基づくMamba2の不規則なブロードキャスト演算と疎計算を対象に、演算子融合フレームワークと疎な事前定義フェッチャ、再構成可能なシストリックアレイを備えたFPGAオーバーレイプロセッサで、メモリ律速なSSM実行を直接加速する。
